title: Restaurant review: Zielona Kuchnia
text:
If you're looking for a vegetarian restaurant in Gdańsk, you have probably heard of Zielona Kuchnia. It opened last year in a small street near the old town, and it's already one of the most popular places in the city. Last Friday I finally went there with two friends to see if it deserves its reputation.

First, the atmosphere. The restaurant is small but bright, with lots of plants, wooden tables and big windows. It was full when we arrived at 7 p.m., so I recommend booking a table, especially at weekends. The staff were friendly and explained the menu patiently – which was useful, because some dishes have quite unusual names.

Now, the food. For starters, we shared beetroot hummus with homemade bread, which was delicious. For my main course I chose a mushroom risotto, and it was one of the best I have ever eaten: creamy, rich and full of flavour. My friends were less lucky. One of them ordered a vegetable curry, which was much too spicy for her, and the other said his burger was a bit dry.

The desserts, however, were perfect. The chocolate cake with raspberries is worth the visit on its own.

The only real problem was the service. Although the waiters were friendly, we waited almost forty minutes for our main courses, and nobody apologised. Prices are also quite high for a vegetarian restaurant – our dinner for three cost 380 złoty.

Overall, I'd give Zielona Kuchnia four stars out of five. It's a great place for a special occasion, but don't go there if you're in a hurry.
